related_questions.question: What paperwork do you need when you retire?
related_questions.snippet: Documents we may ask for include: Your Social Security card or a record of your number. Your original birth certificate, a copy certified by the issuing agency, or other proof of your age. We must see the original document(s), or copies certified by the agency that issued them.
related_questions.title: Retirement | What Documents Will You Need When You Apply? - SSA

related_questions.question: What is the $1000 a month rule for retirement?
related_questions.snippet: One of those is the $1,000 per month rule, a quick way to estimate how much to save based on your expected monthly income needs in retirement. The idea is that for every $1,000 you want to withdraw each month, you'll need about $240,000 saved. That figure assumes a 5% annual withdrawal rate.
related_questions.title: What Is the $1K Per Month Rule in Retirement? - US News Money

related_questions.question: What are the two main forms of retirement plans?
related_questions.snippet: There are two basic types of retirement plans typically offered by employers – defined benefit plans and defined contribution plans. In a defined benefit plan, the employer establishes and maintains a pension that provides a benefit to plan participants (employees) at retirement.
related_questions.title: Employer Retirement Plans: Two Basic Types - Wiser Women

related_questions.question: How many months in advance should I apply for Social Security retirement?
related_questions.snippet: You can apply up to 4 months before you want your retirement benefits to start. If you're not ready to begin receiving retirement benefits, but are thinking about doing so soon, visit our website at www.ssa.gov/benefits/retirement to learn more.
